name: Pulse band (our own wearable)
what: A screenless band with the Pulse logo: heart rate, HRV, sleep and blood oxygen, linked to the Pulse app.
faq: Which factory makes Hume's products?
Hume's Body Pod scale: US customs records show it shipped from Shenzhen Unique Scales. Hume's band: not found. No customs record, FCC filing or teardown names its maker.
Which factory makes the best bands?
For a WHOOP-style band with our logo: J-Style. Top quality: Zepp (made the Xiaomi Mi Band), but it may not take small orders. For a real medical blood-oxygen claim: Viatom (FDA-cleared).
Who makes WHOOP and Oura?
Not public. WHOOP's FCC filing is under WHOOP itself. Oura says it makes in Finland and elsewhere, not China. Ultrahuman builds in Texas and India.
Can we copy the WHOOP look?
No. WHOOP has sued Chinese lookalike bands and won. Get our own design and an IP promise in the contract.
Do we need FDA approval?
Not for wellness (heart rate, HRV, sleep, general SpO2) with no disease claims. Anything like “detects AFib” or “sleep apnea” needs an FDA 510(k).
What else does it need for the US?
An FCC ID (it uses Bluetooth), battery shipping papers (UN38.3), and a silicone strap tested for Prop 65. The FCC may stop accepting some mainland-China test labs, so ask which lab tested it.
Where does member data go?
Must be our own US server, through an SDK. No band vendor we found promises to keep data out of China, so put it in the contract.
How many do we have to buy?
Usually 500+ units with our logo (J-Style says 500 for rings). Ask each one.

neko.note: Neko doesn't make a band. It only imports sleep, steps and HRV from Apple Health. Our own band would go further than Neko here.

name: Pulse smart scale (like Hume Body Pod)
what: A body-composition scale with our logo that syncs to the Pulse app. Optional add-on to the band.
us: Hume Body Pod: retail price varies
faq: Who makes Hume's scale?
US customs records show Shenzhen Unique Scales shipping scales to Hume Health. It's the strongest lead, but neither company has confirmed it.
Is it a medical device?
Not if it's sold for wellness (weight, body fat, muscle). No disease claims.

neko.note: Neko measures body fat and visceral fat with its own imaging device (added June 2026). A smart scale's estimate is much rougher. Good for daily tracking at home, not as a scan replacement.

name: Face skin analyzer
what: Photographs the face to show spots, pores and wrinkles.
faq: Is a $2,000 Chinese one as good as the $7,000+ VISIA?
The photos can be close. VISIA's edge is its skin-comparison database and US service. Ask for a side-by-side demo on your own face, then compare the reports.
Can we use it on members?
Yes, as a photo and education tool. Never call the result a diagnosis.
Any hidden costs?
Ask if the software needs a yearly license or a Chinese server, and what a replacement camera costs.

neko.note: Neko photographs the whole body (2,000+ images, plus heat and depth sensors) to track every mole. This analyzer does the face only. The close match is the Canfield Vectra whole-body system (4/5), which we buy in the US.

usNote: Google Shopping listings, Oct 15, 2026. Some may be the same Chinese machine with a US brand on it.
nego: 美国卖家卖3000到8900美元。你们的出厂价是多少？
US sellers charge $3,000–8,900. What is your factory price?

name: 3D body scanner
what: Rotating scan of body shape for the monthly re-scan.
faq: Do members' scans leave the building?
Ask where scans are stored. Health data on a Chinese server is a problem for a US clinic. Best: data on our own computer or a US server.
Is there a monthly fee?
Fit3D charges about $100 a month. Ask if Visbody's software is a subscription.
How much room does it need?
Ask for the floor space, ceiling height and weight limit of the turntable.

neko.note: Shows body shape, measurements and an estimated body fat. Neko measures visceral fat with its own imaging, so this is a partial match.

name: Handheld heart ultrasound
what: Quick heart look when a scan flags something. Chinese brand, buy from its US dealer.
faq: Why not buy it straight from China?
Warranty, service and the FDA paperwork run through the US office. A direct import can be held at customs.
Which probe do we need for the heart?
A cardiac (phased-array) probe. In Chinese: 相控阵探头 (xiàngkòngzhèn tàntóu).
Who is allowed to scan?
Whoever the medical director approves. Check before buying.

neko.note: Neko appears to run full heart ultrasound with trained echo specialists (from its job ads). A handheld probe gives a quick look, not the same detail.

name: 12-lead ECG (heart tracing)
what: The standard heart tracing, done at every scan. Chinese brands with US clearance, sold by US dealers.
faq: Why not buy it straight from China?
Only US-labeled units with US service are safe to use on patients. FDA can hold imports without the right paperwork.
Edan or Contec?
Edan: FDA-cleared (K102830, K171942) and has a US office. Contec: cleared too (K131900) and cheaper, but no US dealer found.
Does Neko do this?
Yes, Neko does an ECG at every scan.

neko.note: Neko records an ECG at every scan. A 12-lead ECG is the clinical standard, so this matches or beats it.

name: Vital-signs monitor
what: Blood pressure, blood oxygen and temperature in one quick check.
faq: Which one?
Edan iM3 (FDA K180380) from Edan USA. Note: some newer iM3s units had a recall in 2026. Ask if the unit is fixed.
A cheap backup?
Contec CMS50D fingertip oxygen meter (FDA K082641), or Viatom (Wellue) devices sold in the US.
Does it do ankle pressure like Neko?
No. The ankle-arm test needs a separate machine, and no Chinese one has FDA clearance. Buy Mesi or Huntleigh in the US.

neko.note: Neko takes blood pressure on both arms and both ankles. This covers the arms and oxygen; the ankle part needs a separate US-bought machine.

name: Grip strength meter
what: Squeeze test for muscle strength, a strong sign of healthy aging. Neko does it at every scan.
faq: Is a $40 one good enough?
Studies compared the Camry EH101 with the Jamar (the clinic standard): readings were very close (about 2 kg lower on average).
Where to buy?
In the US (IntegratedMedSys or Amazon). Easy and low risk. Keep one Jamar if you want to compare with research.

neko.note: Same measurement Neko takes. A clinical grip meter measures exactly the same thing.

name: IV recliners (4)
what: Reclining chairs for the IV lounge.
faq: Electric or manual?
Electric needs a UL or ETL mark. Manual skips that and costs less.
What matters for cleaning?
Wipeable medical vinyl, few seams, removable arm pads.
What else to ask?
Weight limit, lie-flat position (if someone faints), and locking wheels.

neko.note: Neko is a scan-only clinic: no IV, spa or recovery. This is where Pulse is different from Neko, not a copy of it.

name: Medical fridge with alarm
what: Keeps IV vitamins and Botox cold. Buy the US 115V model from a US dealer.
faq: Why not import one?
Same price as the US dealer, and the US model is already 115V and listed. No reason to import.
What makes it 'medical'?
A digital temperature log and an alarm. Ask for a model that meets CDC vaccine-storage guidance.

neko.note: Neko is a scan-only clinic: no IV, spa or recovery. This is where Pulse is different from Neko, not a copy of it.

name: Saunas
what: Traditional and infrared rooms for the thermal floor.
faq: What's the biggest risk?
The heater and controls. Without a UL or ETL listing, the NJ inspector won't sign off.
Can we buy just the room from China?
Often the smart move: a Chinese wooden cabin with a US-listed heater and controls. Ask if they'll sell the cabin without the heater.
How long until it arrives?
Usually 30–60 days to build plus 30–40 days by sea. Confirm in writing.

neko.note: Neko is a scan-only clinic: no IV, spa or recovery. This is where Pulse is different from Neko, not a copy of it.

name: Hydro pools and spa
what: Two 7×10 ft hydro pools and the round spa. NJ health department must approve the plans.
faq: What do the NJ rules need?
Health department plan approval for a spa used by the public, and pool pumps and filters usually need NSF/ANSI 50 for public pools.
Who installs and repairs it?
Ask if they have a US installer or service partner. If not, find one before ordering.
What else to ask?
The heater and pump wattage, and whether every electrical part is UL or ETL listed.

neko.note: Neko is a scan-only clinic: no IV, spa or recovery. This is where Pulse is different from Neko, not a copy of it.

name: Cold plunge chillers
what: Chillers and tubs for the four cold plunges.
faq: What has to be certified?
The chiller (it's electrical): UL or ETL. Ask how the water is kept clean (ozone, UV, filter).
Do they make for US brands?
Ask which ones, then Harris checks it on ImportYeti (US customs records).
What's the running cost?
Ask the power draw in watts and the noise level.

neko.note: Neko is a scan-only clinic: no IV, spa or recovery. This is where Pulse is different from Neko, not a copy of it.

name: Red light bed
what: Full-body LED bed. Phase 2. Only with a real FDA number.
faq: Is it a medical device?
Light beds sold for wrinkles or pain need an FDA 510(k). Without a K-number, it's a no for 510 Summit.
What power does it need?
Big beds draw a lot. Ask the watts and whether it needs a 240V circuit.
How long do the lights last?
Ask the LED lifetime in hours and the price of a replacement panel.

neko.note: Neko is a scan-only clinic: no IV, spa or recovery. This is where Pulse is different from Neko, not a copy of it.

name: Compression boots
what: Leg recovery for the lounge and recovery room.
faq: Can we sell recovery with these?
Yes, for recovery and wellness. Medical claims (swelling, clots) need FDA clearance.
What wears out?
The leg sleeves. Ask the price of spare sleeves and how they're cleaned.

name: Treatment and blood-draw chairs
faq: Electric or manual?
Electric needs a UL or ETL mark. Manual skips that.
What makes a good blood-draw chair?
Arms that lock, can tip back if someone faints, wipeable vinyl.

neko.note: Not a measurement, but Neko also takes a blood sample at every scan (results in about 30 minutes). The blood-draw chair supports that part.
